images.title: 42 in rows of 7: groups of 14 fit, groups of 28 do not
images.purpose: Shows that a multiple of 7 is divisible by another multiple of 7 only sometimes: 42 splits into groups of 14 but not into groups of 28.
images.composition: Plain white background, lots of empty space around the main object, no scenery, no characters, no extra text. Two identical dot arrays side by side, one grouped in 14s and one grouped in 28s.
images.exact_structure: Two copies of the same array: 6 rows of 7 dots, 42 dots each. Above both, centred: 42 = 7 × 6. Left copy: all dots teal (#0072B2); rows 1 and 2, rows 3 and 4, rows 5 and 6 are each enclosed in a rounded outline, 3 outlines; above it: groups of 14; below it: 3 groups, none left. Right copy: rows 1 to 4 are amber (#E69F00) and enclosed in one rounded outline; rows 5 and 6 are vermilion (#D55E00) and not enclosed; above it: groups of 28; below it: 14 left over. All dots the same size. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec

images.takeaway: 42 is divisible by 14 but not by 28: a multiple of 7 is divisible by 7m only when m is a factor of 6.

image_decisions.why: Regrouping the same rows of 7 shows exactly when a multiple of 7 divides another multiple of 7.
